newsitem.title: UK: OFWAT sees benefits from Chester merger.
newsitem.headline: OFWAT sees benefits from Chester merger.

text.p: Britain's water regulator said on Wednesday that customers of Wrexham Water and Chester Water Plc would see a reduction in their bills if the proposed merger between the two companies went ahead.
Dee Valley Water Plc, the holding company for Wrexham Water, announced earlier that it has made a recommended offer for Chester Water, valuing it at 20.3 million stg.

The companies said they had agreed with the Office of Water Services (OFWAT) that from April 1, 2001, bills for customers of both Dee Valley and Chester Water would be reduced by 3.5 percent over and above the combined existing K factors.
"K" factors are pricing formulas set by OFWAT to determine prices charged by the water companies to customers.

Ian Byatt, director general of OFWAT said in a statement, "The reduction in bills relates only to the merger. I will be reviewing all company price limits in 1999 so these reductions are over and above any reductions to price limits which would otherwise have resulted from my price review."
"This is good news for customers which I welcome".
OFWAT said the assets of each of the companies are below the 30 million stg threshold which triggers an automatic reference to Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
It said it expected to see the merged company able to operate more efficiently than the two companies do at present.
